en.title: C Function Calls — Nested Parity Output
en.description:
The original problem gives a C function that returns 0 for an odd input and 1 for an even input, and calls it twice in a row starting from i=3. This site keeps the function and the number of calls, but reads the initial i from input and outputs the value after the second call.

The input protocol and the generalized ranges are additions by this site; they do not mean the original problem used stdin/stdout.
en.input: One line with one signed 32-bit integer i.
en.output: Output the integer result after calling the original function twice in a row.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the approach, correctness, and complexity.
hints: Trace the state changes step by step; pay special attention to when the increment in the loop condition happens and to the execution order of finally.
